title: Second-warmest December confirms 2024 as the warmest year | Copernicus
text:
Second-warmest December confirms 2024 as the warmest year | Copernicus

 Second-warmest December confirms 2024 as the warmest year 

 Date: 16th January 2025 

December ended the year officially establishing 2024 as the hottest year on record, and the first year above 1.5°C, the global warming temperature threshold set by the 2015 Paris Agreement. According to the dataset of the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S), 2024 was 1.60°C above the estimated 1850-1900 average used to define the pre-industrial level and surpassed 2023 – previously the warmest year ever recorded – by 0.12°C. 

## Surface air temperature anomalies in December 2024 

Globally, December 2024 was 0.76°C warmer than the 1991-2020 average for December, with an average surface air temperature of 13.42°C, making it the second-warmest December on record after December 2023. The temperature was 1.69°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial December average for 1850-1900.

December 2024 also marked the 17 th month in an 18-month period where the global-average surface air temperature was more than 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

Global-average surface air temperature anomalies relative to the 1850–1900 pre-industrial reference period for each December, all months, and running 12-month averages from 1979 to 2024. Use the grey and yellow toggles to change the temporal sampling. Data source: ERA5. Credit: C3S/ECMWF.

In Europe, surface air temperature anomalies were contrasted in December 2024 compared to the 1991-2020 climatological values. North-western Russia exceeded 4°C above normal while many regions in north-western, central, and eastern Europe were 2 to 3°C above average. Southern Norway was up to 4°C above average, whereas the far north experienced temperatures 1°C below normal.

Outside Europe, western Siberia had the highest anomalies, over 10°C above average. Antarctica and North America also experienced above-average temperatures, particularly around Hudson Bay. The southern hemisphere reported heatwaves in parts of Africa, and Australia recorded its third warmest December and second warmest year. Conversely, temperatures were significantly below average in Greenland, central Asia, central-southern South America and central-northern Africa.

Globe and Europe. Surface air temperature anomaly for December 2024 relative to the December average for the period 1991-2020. Data source: ERA5. Credit: C3S/ECMWF.

The average sea surface temperature (SST) for December 2024 was 20.58°C, 0.40°C above the 1991-2020 average, the second highest on record for December. Read the December 2024 surface air temperature update in full

## Contrasting rainfall conditions around the world 

December 2024 witnessed predominantly dry conditions across significant portions of western and central Europe, with notable dryness in the Iberian Peninsula, southern United Kingdom, and northern Italy. However, northern coastal Europe, including Scotland and Norway, experienced above-average rainfall, contributing to localized flooding events. Southeastern Europe also recorded higher-than-normal precipitation, indicating a varied hydrological landscape across the continent.

Globally, wetter-than-average conditions were observed in parts of central and northern United States, Canada, northeastern and western Australia, northeastern Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil. Additionally, Tropical Cyclone Chido caused severe flooding and damage in Mayotte and in southeast Africa in December, highlighting the month's extreme hydrological impact. In contrast, drier conditions prevailed across north-central and southeastern United States, northern Africa, Asia, and southern regions of Africa and America.

## Record-low Arctic sea ice extent 

In December 2024, Arctic sea ice reached its lowest monthly extent for December n the 46-year dataset at 8% below average, exceeding the previous record of 2016 (-7%). The region experienced well below-average sea ice concentrations, especially in areas like Hudson Bay, the northern Barents Sea, and the western Kara Sea, where concentrations were well below average. By 31 December, the daily sea ice extent ranked second lowest for this date, at 12.52 million km2.

The average Antarctic sea ice extent in December 2024 was 10.1 million km2, which is 0.9 million km2 (or about 8%) below the 1991–2020 average for December. This is the 10th lowest extent for December within the 46-year satellite record and contrasts with November, which saw a record-low extent for the month.

## Hydrological variables 

This series of monthly maps and charts, based on ERA5 data, covers several variables: precipitation, humidity, and soil moisture for Europe and the extra-tropical regions. 

Every month, the Copernicus Climate Change Service provides an update on temperatures, hydrology and sea ice, showing the current condition of the climate. The Climate Bulletins include charts and maps with the evolution of key climate change indicators, mainly based on C3S’s reanalysis dataset ERA5.
